title: Research
text:
TipIn one sentence



I fossilize modern microbes in the lab, to help recognise them in ancient rocks and on other planets.

title: Research
text:
Why it matters
Correctly identifying ancient fossils, and linking them to the environments they lived in, lets us reconstruct past conditions on Earth and judge the habitability of other planets. False positives (minerals that look biological) are among the biggest problems in the search for early and extraterrestrial life. Experiments with known starting material are one of the few ways to calibrate what we see.

title: Research
text:
Approach




Grow
Enrichments and pure cultures of sulfur-oxidizing and iron-oxidizing bacteria forming mats, sheaths and stalks.





Mineralize
Encrust the biomass with iron (oxyhydr)oxides, iron sulfides and silica under anoxic, controlled chemistry.





Cook
Experimental diagenesis in hydrothermal and HPHT autoclaves, simulating burial and low-grade metamorphism.





Analyse
SEM-EDX, µRaman, µXRD, FTIR, SIMS, lipid biomarkers and synchrotron imaging to see what survived.

text:

Iron-oxidizers as hidden sources of pyrite microfossils
Tubular sheaths and twisted stalks of iron-oxidizing bacteria, pyritized during experimental diagenesis, as an overlooked origin of pyrite microfossils.

Iron-rich stalactites and Mars
Geomicrobiology of iron-rich cave stalactites, and what it implies for the habitability of iron-rich deposits on Mars.

title: Hrvoje Višić
text:
About me

I am a geomicrobiologist from Croatia, doing my PhD in the Geomicrobiology Group at the University of Tübingen, as part of a DFG Emmy Noether project.

Bacteria have lived on Earth for more than three billion years, but they rarely leave clear fossils. I grow mats of sulfur- and iron-cycling bacteria, then “cook” them under hot, high-pressure conditions like those deep in the Earth’s crust, to see which of their shapes and chemical traces survive. Knowing what a fossilized microbe looks like helps us read the oldest rocks on Earth, and tells rover missions what to look for on Mars.
My path here went from environmental sciences in Zagreb (my bachelor thesis already asked whether Mars was once habitable), through North Pacific plankton, sea-turtle microbiomes and zebrafish ecotoxicology, to experimental fossilization.
